text:
Kavya Rao: Thanks everyone for coming to the runtime roadmap portion. Wanted to capture a few follow-ups from leadership Q&A here so we can track.
Michael Chen: Quick ask — can you share the expected latency SLO targets for the next quarter? I caught 90th p95 numbers but want the concrete goals.
Kavya Rao: Topline: hosted p95 gen latency target 120ms for 8k context steady-state; dedicated SLA target 100ms p95 for committed instances. We also want p99 guardrails but those are more ops-focused.
Anna Lee: Are those numbers for quantized models only or include fp16 variants?
Kavya Rao: They reflect our standard serving profiles (int8/4bit quantized variants) unless customers pin an fp16 build. Note: fp16 paths usually add ~10-20ms on current kernels.
Leo Gutierrez: On batching: what's the plan for dynamic vs static batch sizes? We had some regressions with the old dynamic batching heuristic.
Kavya Rao: We want hybrid. Primary runtime heuristic remains latency-first: target batch until either max_batch_size or latency_budget_ms hit. Secondary path: workload-based dynamic extra-batching for low-latency-tolerant customers (configurable per-route). Ops will flip a canary to increase dynamic aggressiveness by +25% for a subset.
Michael Chen: Can we get the config snippet for the latency budget heuristic? I want to test locally.
Anna Lee: +1
Leo Gutierrez: Also need clarity on KV cache eviction policy — some customers saw worse tails when we cleared prefixes aggressively.
Kavya Rao: Good call. Action: Engineering to publish the planned eviction policy here and a short rationale. Short version: prefer LRU per-client with TTL and a small (configurable) global pressure eviction that protects recent prefixes. We'll also expose a metrics tag for eviction_count and eviction_reason.
Michael Chen: That sounds good. For profiling, can we get per-kernel breakdowns (matmul vs softmax vs attention) in the Console traces? Right now traces group a lot together.
Kavya Rao: Research/Runtime team will add kernel-level spans to Console tracing over the next sprint. Expected field names: kernel_name, kernel_ms, and kernel_device. We'll run it behind a feature flag.
sre-oncall: Any updates on graceful fallback behavior when a kernel hotpatch fails? We saw a canary that rolled back but left some requests hanging.
Leo Gutierrez: We instrumented a safe-fallback path in v0.9.4 that should route to a compatible kernel variant. If the hotpatch leaves hung ops it's likely a coordination bug. I want the trace ids.
Anna Lee: I have two example trace ids from the incident: trace-2026-11-03-014 and trace-2026-11-03-019.
Leo Gutierrez: thanks—I'll pick those up.
Michael Chen: Any timeline for the kernel vectorization work (AOT kernels for attention)? That would shave a lot off the p95.
Kavya Rao: Prioritized for Q2; internal ETA in weeks: planning(2), prototype(3), canary(4). We'll share a roadmap doc and perf estimates soon.
Anna Lee: Can we get a concise checklist of what teams need to do to be ready for the rollout? e.g., model validation, custom ops, rollout flags.
Kavya Rao: Yep — I'll post a checklist here by EOD. High-level items: 1) validate model compatibility with new kernels; 2) run eval suite and baselines; 3) update per-route batch configs if relying on old heuristics; 4) opt-in canary flags and monitor kernel_failure_rate.
deploy-bot: deployment started: runtime/kernel-aot-prototype -> canary group alpha (job 8673) :rocket:
sre-oncall: tagging this for release-war-room FYI — we'll watch latency and error budgets during the canary window.
Kavya Rao: Thanks. Action items captured: Michael to test latency budget locally, Leo to investigate hang traces, Runtime to publish eviction policy + kernel spans, Kavya to post rollout checklist. If anyone needs me ping me directly or drop notes here.
Michael Chen: I'll drop the local config as a gist in #eng-runtime later today.
Anna Lee: thanks!
Leo Gutierrez: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
